<a id="meter"></a><a id="package-meter"></a>

## Package meter

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/meter"`

Package meter counts what a verified capability uses — requests and spend, against the capability's ceilings, its ancestors', its Biscuit copies' and its tenant's — and keeps the charges ledger, for billing and reports.

limes verifies a capability and hands the meter what to count it against, [limes.VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject](verifying.md#limes.VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject); nothing in limes depends on this package, so a consumer that only verifies tokens never imports it. The refusals a ceiling answers with — [limes.ErrRequestLimitExceeded](errors.md#limes.ErrRequestLimitExceeded), [limes.ErrBudgetExceeded](errors.md#limes.ErrBudgetExceeded), [limes.ErrTenantBudgetExceeded](errors.md#limes.ErrTenantBudgetExceeded) — are limes's, so [limes.Verifier.ErrorResponse](verifying.md#limes.Verifier.ErrorResponse) answers a metering refusal as it answers a verification one. A call for a tenant whose usage was erased is refused with [limes.ErrTenantErased](errors.md#limes.ErrTenantErased), a kind of [limes.ErrRevoked](errors.md#limes.ErrRevoked). Every error of the meter's names its code, so [limes.CodeOf](errors.md#limes.CodeOf), [limes.CategoryOf](errors.md#limes.CategoryOf) and [limes.ProblemOf](errors.md#limes.ProblemOf) answer it as one of limes's.

#### What you implement

[UsageStore](#meter.UsageStore) — request and spend counters and the charges ledger; the union of [Meter](#meter.Meter), [MeterReader](#meter.MeterReader), [TenantBudgets](#meter.TenantBudgets) and [UsageHousekeeping](#meter.UsageHousekeeping). Every charge and request also counts against each ancestor, and every Biscuit copy with limits of its own against the copy quota of the capability and of each ancestor; see "Transactions" below. More are needed only with the feature they serve: [CopyUsageReader](#meter.CopyUsageReader) to show a Biscuit copy's own counters, [LedgerReader](#meter.LedgerReader) to sum a tenant's charges, [LedgerHousekeeping](#meter.LedgerHousekeeping) to remove charges past [MinChargeRetention](#meter.MinChargeRetention), [MatchingReleaser](#meter.MatchingReleaser) to free at once the holds of capabilities a bulk revocation stopped, [Leaser](#meter.Leaser) to lease a capability its budget, and [TenantUsageEraser](#meter.TenantUsageEraser) to remove a tenant. memstore ships them in memory, pgstore over PostgreSQL, and metertest checks any implementation. [Features](#meter.Features) names the optional ones a store implements and has on — a [FeatureGate](#meter.FeatureGate) says which its configuration turned off — and [Require](#meter.Require) refuses at startup a store, or a decorator over one, that lacks one the consumer uses; [As](#meter.As) does so and hands back the interface, as meter.As\[meter.Leaser](store), [AsAll](#meter.AsAll) does it for several at once, naming every one missing, and [AsOptional](#meter.AsOptional) for one the consumer runs without when its configuration turned it off.

#### Transactions

Meter.Charge and Meter.Settle take an onCharged callback that runs inside the charge, receiving the charge's receipt (Charged) and a context that carries the store's transaction, so a side effect such as an outbox write commits atomically with the spend and names the charge. The transaction is onCharged's to write through while it runs, and the store's to end: onCharged never commits or rolls it back. The store puts its transaction there and reads it back with an accessor of its own — pgstore.TxFrom — so neither the contract nor a caller holding a UsageStore names a transaction type, and one service can meter through stores of different kinds. That is what keeps this package free of any database dependency.

A store with no transactions, such as memstore, hands onCharged the caller's context. Everything else behaves identically; only the atomic-side-effect guarantee is forgone, and that limitation is store-dependent rather than a degradation of the primitive.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.MinChargeRetention"></a>

### meter.MinChargeRetention

```go
const MinChargeRetention = billingYear + disputeWindow
```

MinChargeRetention is the least a ledger keeps a charge: until then the charge's ExternalRef replays it rather than charging again, its settled hold replays its receipt, Refund finds it, and SumCharges counts it. A ledger may remove a charge older than its retention, which is no shorter than this, and those promises then lapse for it. Removing charges by hand is held to it too. Erasing a tenant (TenantUsageEraser) is not: it removes every charge of the tenant, whatever its age. Its value holds for all of v1: raising or lowering it moves what PurgeCharges accepts (docs/adr/0002-ledger-retention.md).

<a id="meter.ErrCounterOverflow"></a><a id="meter.ErrChargeNotFound"></a><a id="meter.ErrRefundExceedsCharge"></a><a id="meter.ErrReservationNotFound"></a><a id="meter.ErrCopyLimitExceeded"></a><a id="meter.ErrUsageNotFound"></a><a id="meter.ErrTenantBudgetNotFound"></a><a id="meter.ErrTenantBudgetVersionMismatch"></a>

### meter.ErrCounterOverflow, meter.ErrChargeNotFound, meter.ErrRefundExceedsCharge, meter.ErrReservationNotFound, meter.ErrCopyLimitExceeded, meter.ErrUsageNotFound, meter.ErrTenantBudgetNotFound, meter.ErrTenantBudgetVersionMismatch

```go
var (
	// ErrCounterOverflow — an amount, each valid on its own, that would take
	// a counter past MaxNanos. The request is well formed; the counter has
	// no room for it.
	ErrCounterOverflow error = &familyError{"limes: counter would pass MaxNanos", nil, CodeCounterOverflow}

	// ErrChargeNotFound — Refund, GetCharge or ChargeByRef named a charge
	// with no ledger row.
	ErrChargeNotFound error = &familyError{"limes: charge not found", limes.ErrNotFound, CodeChargeNotFound}

	// ErrRefundExceedsCharge — Refund would return more than the charge
	// took, counting earlier refunds of the same charge.
	ErrRefundExceedsCharge error = &familyError{"limes: refund exceeds charge", nil, CodeRefundExceedsCharge}

	// ErrReservationNotFound — Settle named a reservation that does not
	// exist, was released, or has expired. One already settled is not an
	// error: Settle returns its charge again (ChargeReceipt.Replayed).
	ErrReservationNotFound error = &familyError{"limes: reservation not found", limes.ErrNotFound, CodeReservationNotFound}

	// ErrCopyLimitExceeded — counting one more Biscuit copy of the
	// capability would pass the copy quota of the capability or of an
	// ancestor (limes.Caveats.Copies), or the store's bound of copies per
	// capability (Meter, "Copies of a Biscuit"). The request is refused and nothing is
	// counted. Matches ErrRequestLimitExceeded: the capability has used what
	// it may.
	ErrCopyLimitExceeded error = &familyError{"limes: copy limit exceeded", limes.ErrRequestLimitExceeded, CodeCopyLimitExceeded}

	// ErrUsageNotFound — no usage row exists for this capability.
	// Get-only; bump/charge always inserts on first hit.
	ErrUsageNotFound error = &familyError{"limes: usage row not found", limes.ErrNotFound, CodeUsageNotFound}

	// ErrTenantBudgetNotFound — Get-only; the tenant has no ceiling set
	// and has never been charged. A tenant charged before any ceiling was
	// set has a row, Unlimited, with ResourceVersion 0.
	ErrTenantBudgetNotFound error = &familyError{"limes: tenant budget row not found", limes.ErrNotFound, CodeTenantBudgetNotFound}

	// ErrTenantBudgetVersionMismatch — SetTenantBudget's OCC guard refused the
	// write: the stored resource_version is not the one the caller read, so
	// someone else changed the cap in between. The caller re-reads and decides,
	// rather than silently overwriting a change it never saw. Matches
	// ErrConflict.
	ErrTenantBudgetVersionMismatch error = &familyError{"limes: tenant budget resource_version mismatch", limes.ErrConflict, CodeTenantBudgetVersionMismatch}
)
```

The meter's own sentinels. The refusals ErrorResponse answers — limes.ErrRequestLimitExceeded, limes.ErrBudgetExceeded, limes.ErrTenantBudgetExceeded — and limes.ErrInvalidAmount stay in limes, beside the rest of its error families.

<sub>[meter/errors.go](../../meter/errors.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.ErrExternalRefConflict"></a>

### meter.ErrExternalRefConflict

```go
var ErrExternalRefConflict error = &familyError{"limes: external ref already names a different charge", limes.ErrConflict, CodeExternalRefConflict}
```

ErrExternalRefConflict — Charge named an ExternalRef its capability already charged under, for a different amount, unit or tenant, or under other Biscuit copies. One reference names one cost; replaying the first receipt would report the second as booked. The error names the reference, never the charge it names. Matches ErrConflict: the request is well formed, and would have charged had the reference been free.

### meter.ErrLeasingDisabled

```go

```

ErrLeasingDisabled — Lease of a store whose operator disabled leasing (pgstore's Config.DisableLeases) while an instance writing its database runs a release that knows no leases. <sub>[meter/errors.go](../../meter/errors.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.ErrOutcomeUnknown"></a>

### meter.ErrOutcomeUnknown

```go
var ErrOutcomeUnknown error = &familyError{"limes: the store lost the answer to the call's commit", nil, CodeOutcomeUnknown}
```

ErrOutcomeUnknown — a store sent the call's commit and lost the answer: the connection failed, or the context ended, after the commit left and before the database replied. The call may have committed or not. The error wraps the cause beside it, so errors.Is matches both. Only a call keyed to its cost can be sent again safely: Charge with an ExternalRef, Reserve with a ReservationID, Refund with a RefundID, and Settle; a repeat of one that committed replays it. Matches no family: it is no refusal, and the call is neither wrong nor known to have failed.

<a id="meter.ErrTenantBudgetBusy"></a>

### meter.ErrTenantBudgetBusy

```go
var ErrTenantBudgetBusy error = &familyError{"limes: the tenant's calls in flight held its budget too long", nil, CodeTenantBudgetBusy}
```

ErrTenantBudgetBusy — SetTenantBudget waits for every metered call of the tenant in flight before it changes the ceiling, and gave up after a bound the store sets, changing nothing (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md, Decision 9). The call may be sent again. Matches no family: the request is neither wrong nor in conflict with what is on record, and the store did not fail.

<a id="meter.AllChargeSums"></a>

### meter.AllChargeSums

```go
func AllChargeSums(ctx context.Context, l LedgerReader, req SumChargesRequest) iter.Seq2[ChargeSum, error]
```

AllChargeSums walks SumCharges page by page, from req.Cursor, and yields every sum in its order, as AllTenantBudgets does. A charge or a refund made during the walk moves a sum between pages, so a group may be yielded twice or not at all; see LedgerReader.SumCharges.

### meter.AllTenantBudgets

```go
func AllTenantBudgets(ctx context.Context, l TenantBudgetLister, req ListTenantBudgetsRequest) iter.Seq2[TenantBudget, error]
```

AllTenantBudgets walks ListTenantBudgets page by page, from req.Cursor, and yields every row in its order, as AllByPrincipal does. Spend moves between pages, so a tenant may be yielded twice or not at all; see TenantBudgets.ListTenantBudgets.

<sub>[meter/pages.go](../../meter/pages.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.As"></a>

### meter.As

```go
func As[T any](s UsageStore) (T, error)
```

As is s as the optional interface T — meter.As\[meter.Leaser](store) — or, as Require refuses, limes.ErrInvalidConfig naming T when s is not one and ErrFeatureDisabled when its configuration turned T's feature off: Require and the type assertion after it, in one call.

ErrFeatureDisabled matches limes.ErrInvalidConfig too, so a caller that stops its start on a build without the interface but runs on without a feature turned off checks ErrFeatureDisabled first; AsOptional does that for it.

<sub>[meter/features.go](../../meter/features.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.AsAll"></a>

### meter.AsAll

```go
func AsAll(s UsageStore, targets ...any) error
```

AsAll sets each target, a pointer to an optional interface, to s, and refuses as Require does, naming every one s is not or has turned off — one call at startup for every interface a consumer uses. Each target it refuses is left as it was, nil for a fresh variable, so its error is always checked. Whether a target is a pointer to an interface is known only when it runs: one that is not is limes.ErrInvalidRequest, and none is set.

<sub>[meter/features.go](../../meter/features.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.AsOptional"></a>

### meter.AsOptional

```go
func AsOptional[T any](s UsageStore) (t T, enabled bool, err error)
```

AsOptional is As for a feature a consumer runs without when the store's configuration turned it off: s as T with enabled true; the zero T, false and no error when it is off; and As's error when s is not T at all, a build to fix. One call beside AsAll for the features it needs:

	leaser, leasing, err := meter.AsOptional[meter.Leaser](store)

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.BudgetMeter"></a>

### meter.BudgetMeter

```go
type BudgetMeter interface {
	// Charge adds req.Amount to the spend counters of the capability, of
	// each ancestor and of the tenant aggregate, writes one charges-ledger
	// row, and runs onCharged — ALL atomically. Checks, in order:
	//
	//   1. Each Biscuit copy's own budget (req.Subject.Copies), innermost
	//      first → ErrBudgetExceeded.
	//   2. The capability's own ceiling (req.Subject.Budget()) →
	//      ErrBudgetExceeded.
	//   3. Each ancestor's ceiling → ErrBudgetExceeded.
	//   4. The tenant aggregate ceiling → ErrTenantBudgetExceeded.
	//
	// Any rejection, or an error from onCharged, leaves every counter and
	// the ledger untouched. onCharged runs inside the charge, atomically
	// with it, once every ceiling has passed. It receives a context carrying
	// the store's transaction, which the store's own accessor reads
	// (pgstore.TxFrom; a store with none hands the caller's context on), and
	// the receipt the call will return (Charged), so
	// a side effect such as an outbox write commits with the spend and names
	// the ChargeID. Whether the ledger row is there yet to read is the
	// store's: pgstore writes it before onCharged runs, memstore after.
	// pgstore does so that what onCharged writes — an outbox row with a
	// foreign key to the ledger, say — sees the charge's row; it costs a
	// round trip, since COMMIT then goes after onCharged rather than with
	// the last writes, and it shortens no lock, which the call holds to
	// COMMIT in either order. Pass
	// nil to skip it. It must not call back into the Meter: an
	// implementation may hold its counters while onCharged runs, so a nested
	// call can wait on itself. A store with transactions runs it inside the
	// locked transaction — the chain's counters and the tenant's aggregate,
	// which every other charge of the tenant waits for — so it is short, and
	// touches only that store's database, through the transaction it is
	// handed: no network call.
	//
	// The returned receipt carries the ledger row's ID; Refund takes it.
	//
	// With req.ExternalRef set, Charge is idempotent on (CapabilityID,
	// ExternalRef): a charge whose pair is already in the ledger moves
	// nothing, does not run onCharged, and returns that charge's receipt
	// with Replayed set — also once the capability is no longer on record,
	// as Settle replays a settled hold — for as long as that charge stays in
	// the ledger: a ledger may remove charges older than a retention of at
	// least MinChargeRetention, and the pair then charges anew. The pair names one cost: arriving again with a
	// different Amount, UnitCode or TenantID, or under other Biscuit copies
	// than req.Subject carries, it returns ErrExternalRefConflict and moves
	// nothing. With req.Overrun = OverrunPolicyRecord, a charge that
	// would cross a ceiling is committed anyway and the receipt reports it
	// (ChargeReceipt.Overrun); see OverrunPolicy.
	//
	// Under a lease that keeps moving while the call locks it, a store may
	// refuse a charge as limes.ErrConflict, moving nothing and running no
	// onCharged; the caller sends it again (Leaser).
	Charge(ctx context.Context, req ChargeRequest, onCharged func(ctx context.Context, c Charged) error) (ChargeReceipt, error)

	// Refund returns spend from one recorded charge to every counter that
	// charge debited (capability, ancestors, tenant aggregate), and records
	// the refund against the charge. req.Remaining refunds whatever
	// remains, which makes a full refund idempotent; a partial refund that
	// would take the total refunded past the charge returns
	// ErrRefundExceedsCharge and changes nothing. An unknown charge ID —
	// never charged, or removed from the ledger past its retention
	// (MinChargeRetention) — returns ErrChargeNotFound, and a request naming neither an Amount nor
	// Remaining, or both, ErrInvalidRequest. The receipt carries the amount
	// actually refunded.
	//
	// A charge counted in a tenant accounting period that has since been
	// closed (SetTenantBudget with ResetSpend) is refunded to the
	// capability, its ancestors and its copies, but not to the tenant
	// aggregate: the current period never counted it.
	// Likewise a counter restarted since the charge (DeleteUsage on a
	// capability still on record) never counted it, and is left alone.
	//
	// With req.RefundID set, Refund is idempotent on it: a refund already
	// on record under the id, of the same charge for the same request — the
	// same Amount, or Remaining again — moves nothing and returns the first
	// receipt, with Replayed set and Amount what that refund returned. The
	// id names one refund: one on record for another charge or another
	// request returns ErrRefundConflict and changes nothing. The key lasts
	// as long as its charge does in the ledger (MinChargeRetention), and
	// goes with it. Without one, a partial refund sent twice refunds twice.
	//
	// onRefunded runs inside the refund, atomically with it, as onCharged
	// runs inside a charge: once the refund's writes are made, before they
	// commit, with a context carrying the store's transaction (read through
	// the store's own accessor, pgstore.TxFrom) and the receipt the call
	// will return (Refunded), so a side effect such as an outbox event
	// commits with the refund. pgstore writes the charge's refunded amount,
	// and a keyed refund's record, before onRefunded runs; memstore after.
	// An error from it leaves every counter, the charge's refunded amount
	// and the RefundID untouched, and is returned. Pass nil to skip it. It
	// must not call back into the Meter, and is short and touches only the
	// store's database, through the transaction it is handed, for the
	// reasons given under Charge. A store that retries a transaction it
	// lost to a deadlock runs it again on the retry, the first run having
	// rolled back with its refund.
	//
	// onRefunded does not run on a replay under req.RefundID, nor when
	// nothing is refunded (Remaining, once nothing remains): a keyed refund
	// of nothing is still recorded, so its retry replays and runs none
	// either. A call that returns ErrOutcomeUnknown is retried under the
	// same RefundID: a first attempt that committed wrote its side effect
	// with it, and the retry replays without running onRefunded; one that
	// did not commit wrote nothing, and the retry refunds and runs it.
	//
	// For a cost only known afterwards, prefer Reserve/Settle: a
	// reservation lapses on its own if the caller never settles it, where
	// an estimate charged up front stays charged.
	Refund(ctx context.Context, req RefundRequest, onRefunded func(ctx context.Context, r Refunded) error) (RefundReceipt, error)

	// Reserve holds req.Amount against the capability, each ancestor and
	// the tenant aggregate, checking every ceiling against spend plus
	// what is already held. Holds count against later charges and
	// reservations exactly as spend does, until the reservation is
	// settled, released or expires. A hold expires req.TTL from now, or with
	// its capability's record if that comes sooner: past it no one can
	// settle the hold. Whether a token has expired is its verifier's to
	// decide, by its own clock and leeway, so a store whose clock is not the
	// verifier's may end the hold up to the leeway past the record's expiry
	// that a verifier may still accept the token for. A capability past
	// that — one a late cost names through StoredMeterSubject — is refused
	// ErrExpired; a store that shares the verifier's clock may refuse it
	// from the record's expiry on.
	// Rejections return the Charge sentinels and hold nothing.
	//
	// With req.ReservationID set, Reserve is idempotent on it: a hold
	// already on record under the id, made for the same request — the same
	// capability, tenant and Biscuit copies, Amount, unit, Op and Actor —
	// moves nothing and is returned as on record, with Replayed set and its
	// ExpiresAt unchanged. The id names one hold: one on record for another
	// request returns ErrReserveConflict and moves nothing, and so does the
	// id of a hold already settled, whose charge carries it. The key holds
	// while the hold, or the charge that settled it, is on record: once the
	// hold is released — by Release, by ReleaseExpired past its expiry, or
	// with its capability's usage — the id may hold anew.
	Reserve(ctx context.Context, req ReserveRequest) (Reservation, error)

	// Settle ends a reservation and charges the actual cost in its place,
	// atomically: the hold is released and req.Amount is charged as
	// Charge would, with onCharged run inside. The actual cost may be
	// below, equal to or above the hold; above it, the excess must fit
	// every ceiling, or Settle returns the Charge sentinel and the
	// reservation stays in place for the caller to settle lower or
	// release — unless req.Overrun is OverrunPolicyRecord, when the cost is
	// charged anyway and the receipt reports it.
	//
	// Settle is idempotent on the reservation: settling one already
	// settled for the same Amount moves nothing, does not run onCharged, and
	// returns the receipt of the charge that settled it, with Replayed set,
	// while that charge stays in the ledger (MinChargeRetention); past it,
	// the reservation is unknown. Settling it again for another Amount returns ErrSettleConflict and
	// moves nothing: the reservation names one cost, and replaying its
	// receipt would report the second as booked. An unknown,
	// released or expired reservation returns ErrReservationNotFound, and so
	// does the zero id, which names none — never a direct charge. So does a
	// reservation made by another capability or tenant, or under other Biscuit copies
	// than req.Subject carries: a hold is settled by the copy that made it,
	// so a copy cannot settle a sibling's hold past its own limits.
	Settle(ctx context.Context, req SettleRequest, onCharged func(ctx context.Context, c Charged) error) (ChargeReceipt, error)

	// Release ends a reservation without charging. Idempotent: releasing
	// one that is gone is a no-op. So is releasing a reservation made by
	// another capability or tenant, or under other Biscuit copies than req.Subject
	// carries: it is none of this subject's, and stays held, so a copy
	// cannot free a sibling's hold to spend past its own limits.
	Release(ctx context.Context, req ReleaseRequest) error
}
```

BudgetMeter enforces the budget ceilings (Caveats.Budget, a tenant's aggregate ceiling) and keeps the charges ledger, as Meter describes them.

<a id="meter.ChargeReceipt"></a>

### meter.ChargeReceipt

```go
type ChargeReceipt struct {
	// ChargeID identifies the ledger row; pass it to Meter.Refund.
	ChargeID uuid.UUID
	// SpentAmount is the capability's spend as this call returns (its subtree's,
	// when it has delegated children).
	SpentAmount limes.Nanos
	// Replayed reports that the charge was already in the ledger — the same
	// ExternalRef, or a reservation already settled — so this call moved
	// nothing and ChargeID names the earlier charge.
	Replayed bool
	// Overrun reports that the charge crossed at least one ceiling, which
	// only OverrunPolicyRecord allows.
	Overrun bool
	// TenantID and UnitCode are the charge's tenant and unit, so a caller
	// holding only the receipt — logged, or passed on — can attribute it. A
	// refusal by a ceiling or by onCharged still sets them.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	UnitCode string
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ChargeReceipt is the result of a committed charge.

### meter.ChargeRecord

```go

	// from it since.

	RefundedAmount limes.Nanos
	UnitCode       string
	// ExternalRef is the charge's ChargeRequest.ExternalRef; empty for none.
	ExternalRef string
	// Overrun reports that the charge crossed a ceiling (OverrunPolicyRecord).
	Overrun bool
	// Op and Actor are what the charge was for and who made it, as the
	// request named them; At is when it was committed.

	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ChargeRecord is one charge as the ledger holds it.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.ChargeRequest"></a>

### meter.ChargeRequest

```go
type ChargeRequest struct {
	// Subject is the capability charged — its tenant, its own ceiling, its
	// unit and the presented copy's limits: VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject.
	// No conversion happens: a counter the charge moves — the
	// capability's, an ancestor's, the tenant's — that already counts in
	// another unit refuses it with ErrUnitCodeMismatch, and so does a
	// reservation.
	Subject limes.MeterSubject
	// Amount is the cost, in the subject's unit. Within 0..MaxNanos
	// (Nanos.Validate).
	Amount limes.Nanos
	// Op and Actor are stamped on the ledger row for attribution only;
	// both may be empty and neither affects enforcement.
	Op    limes.Op
	Actor string
	// ExternalRef names the cost in the consumer's own records — the id of
	// the call or the event that reported it — and makes the charge
	// idempotent on (capability, ExternalRef). Empty: every call charges.
	// At most MaxExternalRefBytes long.
	ExternalRef string
	// Overrun is what happens when Amount would cross a ceiling.
	Overrun OverrunPolicy
}
```

ChargeRequest is the input to Meter.Charge.

	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	// Charged is what the group's charges took; Refunded, what has been
	// returned from them since. Charged less Refunded is the net.

}

ChargeSum is one group's sums. The fields a request did not group by are zero.

type CopyUsageReader interface {

Feature names an optional interface a UsageStore may implement beside the ones it must. 	// FeatureCopyUsage — CopyUsageReader: a Biscuit copy's own counters.
	FeatureCopyUsage Feature = "copy_usage"
	// FeatureTenantUsageErase — TenantUsageEraser: removing a tenant's usage.
	FeatureTenantUsageErase Feature = "tenant_usage_erase"

	// revocation outdates.

	// FeatureTenantReservations — TenantReservationLister: listing a
	// tenant's open reservations.

	// FeatureLeases — Leaser: leasing part of a chain's limits.

)

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.Lease"></a>

### meter.Lease

```go
type Lease struct {
	// ID is this lease's, from the Lease that opened it until it is
	// settled; a lease opened after it — by a top-up among others — has
	// another. A refund of a charge taken under it goes to the lease while
	// it is open, and to the chain once it is settled.
	ID           uuid.UUID
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	TenantID     uuid.UUID
	UnitCode     string
	// Amount is what the lease holds — for one a top-up opened, what the
	// lease before it had left and the top-up; Spent is what its
	// capability and those delegated from it charged under it.
	Amount, Spent limes.Nanos
	// Requests is how many requests the lease holds, counted as Amount is;
	// RequestsSpent how many its capability and those delegated from it
	// made under it.
	Requests, RequestsSpent int64
	// ExpiresAt is when the lease ends unless settled first; a charge
	// after it goes through the whole chain.
	ExpiresAt time.Time
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Lease is the budget a capability holds of its chain: Amount held against every ancestor and the tenant, of which Spent is spent.

### meter.LeaseRequest

```go
type LeaseRequest struct {
	// Subject is the leaseholder (VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject).
	Subject limes.MeterSubject
	// Amount to lease, in the subject's unit. A top-up of an open lease
	// settles it and opens a new one of what it had left and Amount
	// (Leaser.Lease). Within 0..MaxNanos; a lease of no amount covers no
	// Charge.
	Amount limes.Nanos
	// Requests to lease; a top-up's new lease holds what the open one had
	// left and these. A lease of none covers no Bump. Negative is
	// ErrInvalidRequest, and so is a request of no amount and no requests.
	Requests int64
	// TTL is how long the lease lasts unless settled, at most until its
	// capability expires, as a hold's (Meter.Reserve); a top-up's new lease
	// lasts this long from the top-up. 0 = DefaultLeaseTTL; negative is
	// ErrInvalidRequest.
	TTL time.Duration
}
```

LeaseRequest asks for budget a capability holds of its chain in advance (docs/adr/0017-budget-leases.md).

#### meter.LeaseRequest.Validate

```go
func (r LeaseRequest) Validate() error
```

Validate refuses an amount out of range, negative requests, a lease of no amount and no requests, a subject that names no capability, no tenant or no unit, or an unknown unit, a Biscuit copy, and a negative TTL. A copy's charges and bumps never go under a lease, so a lease of one would hold its chain's budget past the copy's own ceilings.

<sub>[meter/lease.go](../../meter/lease.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.Leaser"></a>

### meter.Leaser

```go
type Leaser interface {
	// Lease opens a lease of req.Amount and req.Requests on the subject,
	// refusing what a Reserve of that amount, or as many Bumps, would
	// refuse — a ceiling crossed is the ceiling's sentinel — and
	// ErrLeaseNested under an ancestor that holds one. On a subject that
	// holds an open lease it is a top-up: atomically, under the locks
	// SettleLease takes, the open lease is settled, so what it spent
	// reaches the chain, and a new one opened under a new ID, holding what
	// the old one had left and req's, until req.TTL from now; a refused
	// top-up leaves the open lease as it was. A lease that expired is
	// settled first and a new one of req's alone opened.
	Lease(ctx context.Context, req LeaseRequest) (Lease, error)
	// GetLease returns the lease of capID still holding budget — open, or
	// expired and not yet settled (ExpiresAt tells which) — or
	// ErrLeaseNotFound.
	GetLease(ctx context.Context, capID uuid.UUID) (Lease, error)
	// SettleLease settles the subject's lease and returns it as it ended,
	// or ErrLeaseNotFound when it holds none.
	SettleLease(ctx context.Context, req SettleLeaseRequest) (Lease, error)
}
```

Leaser leases budget and requests to a capability, so that its charges and bumps, and those of the capabilities delegated from it, lock its own counters and not those of its ancestors or its tenant (docs/adr/0017-budget-leases.md). A usage store implements it; memstore's and pgstore's do.

A lease holds its amount against every ancestor and the tenant, and its requests against every ancestor (ReservedRequests), at once, checking every ceiling then, so a charge or a bump under it checks only the capabilities below the leaseholder and the lease's balance; what it spent reaches the chain when it is settled. Every path that does not charge under a lease goes through the whole chain as before, which the held amount keeps correct — it counts against every ceiling until settled:

  - A Charge with OverrunPolicyReject is charged under the lease of its capability, or of its nearest ancestor that holds one, while the lease is open and unexpired; a charge it cannot cover is refused with ErrLeaseExhausted, and the caller leases more. A lease of no amount covers no Charge.
  - A Bump is counted under the lease the same way, while the lease holds requests; one it has none left for is refused with ErrLeaseRequestsExhausted. A lease of no requests covers no Bump.
  - A Charge with OverrunPolicyRecord, a Charge of a Biscuit copy with limits of its own — whose quota counts on every ancestor — a Bump of one, and Reserve, Settle and Release, go through the whole chain.
  - A capability whose ancestor holds an open lease cannot lease (ErrLeaseNested): a lease is drawn from the whole chain. A later minor may let a request opt in to a lease drawn from the ancestor's instead; without that, this refusal holds for all of v1.
  - A Biscuit copy cannot lease (ErrInvalidRequest): none of its calls go under a lease, which would hold its chain's budget past the copy's own ceilings.

A lease is settled — its spend charged to every ancestor and the tenant, its requests counted on every ancestor, the rest released — by SettleLease, by a Lease that tops it up, by ReleaseExpired once it expired, by ReleaseMatching once its capability is revoked, by DeleteUsage and PurgeOrphans before its counters go, by DeleteUsage before an ancestor's go — the hold it keeps on them goes with them — and by a SetTenantBudget that resets the spend, before it does. A Refund of a charge taken under a lease returns it to the lease while it is open, and to the chain once it is settled.

A store that reads a lease before it locks its counters may find the lease moved in between: settled and reopened by a top-up, or settled by SettleLease, ReleaseExpired or another path above. It runs the call again, and past a bound of its own on how often refuses it as limes.ErrConflict, having moved nothing, rather than run for as long as the lease keeps moving. A Charge or a Bump under a lease, a Lease that settles an expired one first, and SettleLease may return it; the call was rejected, so the caller sends it again, keyed or not. pgstore does this; memstore never returns it.

<sub>[meter/lease.go](../../meter/lease.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.LedgerHousekeeping"></a>

### meter.LedgerHousekeeping

```go
type LedgerHousekeeping interface {
	// PurgeCharges removes the charges taken more than req.Retention() ago,
	// by the store's clock, oldest first, at most req.Limit of them, of
	// every tenant the call's scope reaches, and reports how many it
	// removed. A worker calls it until a batch comes back short of the
	// limit. A charge removed takes its promises with it: its ExternalRef
	// charges anew, its settled hold is a reservation not found, Refund
	// and GetCharge answer ErrChargeNotFound, and SumCharges no longer
	// counts it. It refuses what PurgeChargesRequest.Validate refuses.
	PurgeCharges(ctx context.Context, req PurgeChargesRequest) (PurgeChargesResult, error)
}
```

LedgerHousekeeping removes old charges from the ledger, which otherwise grows by a row for every charge for as long as the store lives (ADR-0002). It is a type of its own beside UsageStore, as LedgerReader is: a housekeeping worker holds it. memstore's and pgstore's Ledger are each one; metertest checks it when its Env.Ledger is one and Env.Advance is set.

<sub>[meter/ledger.go](../../meter/ledger.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.LedgerReader"></a>

### meter.LedgerReader

```go
type LedgerReader interface {
	// SumCharges returns one page of sums, each one group's: the charges of
	// req.TenantID, or of every tenant with req.AllTenants, taken in
	// [req.From, req.To) — by the store's clock, as ChargeRecord.At has it
	// — and kept by req.Filter, grouped by unit always, by req.Bucket, and
	// by each dimension in req.GroupBy. Amounts in different units are
	// never summed together. Within a bucket the largest charged come
	// first, so the first page of Limit rows is the top Limit; buckets come
	// in time order. A refund counts in the group of the charge it returns,
	// whenever it is made: a closed period's sums still move. A sum past
	// MaxNanos is ErrCounterOverflow. It sums the charges the ledger still
	// holds: one older than the ledger's retention (MinChargeRetention) may
	// be gone, and a period that old sums what is left of it.
	//
	// A sum across tenants is a read of every tenant's ledger: a store that
	// scopes calls to a tenant refuses it under any narrower scope, a tenant
	// filter included, with limes.ErrScopeMismatch, as it refuses
	// ListTenantBudgets.
	SumCharges(ctx context.Context, req SumChargesRequest) (limes.Page[ChargeSum], error)
}
```

LedgerReader sums the charges ledger over a period, for billing and reporting — one tenant's, or every tenant's: totals, the largest spenders by tenant, operation, actor or capability, and series by hour, day, week or month. It reads the ledger the Meter writes, so a consumer reports from it rather than from a store's tables. It is a type of its own, beside UsageStore rather than one of its interfaces: a reporter holds it, a meter does not. memstore and pgstore each ship one; metertest checks it when its Env sets one.

<a id="meter.MatchingReleaser"></a>

### meter.MatchingReleaser

```go
type MatchingReleaser interface {
	// ReleaseMatching releases at most req's Limit (HousekeepingLimit) open
	// holds, in id order, each of a capability that is revoked and that
	// matches req's selectors or was delegated from one that does,
	// returning each hold's amount to its capability, its ancestors and its
	// tenant as Release does, and reports how many and whether the batch
	// was full. A hold of a live capability is never released: its cost may
	// still come. It refuses what ReleaseMatchingRequest.Validate refuses,
	// a call scoped to another tenant as limes.ErrScopeMismatch, and an
	// AllTenants call under a scope that does not admit writing every
	// tenant as limes.ErrScopeMismatch too.
	ReleaseMatching(ctx context.Context, req ReleaseMatchingRequest) (ReleaseMatchingResult, error)
}
```

MatchingReleaser releases at once the holds of capabilities a bulk revocation stopped, which would otherwise count against the ceilings until they expire (ReleaseExpired). A usage store over the records the revocation wrote implements it; memstore's and pgstore's do.

<sub>[meter/release_matching.go](../../meter/release_matching.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.Meter"></a>

### meter.Meter

```go
type Meter interface {
	RequestCounter
	BudgetMeter
}
```

Meter enforces the request and budget ceilings (Caveats.Requests, Caveats.Budget) and keeps the charges ledger: a RequestCounter and a BudgetMeter together. Separated from Store so the issuance / revocation surface stays focused on identity, not runtime state.

##### Delegation trees

A capability's counters cover its whole subtree: Bump and Charge apply to the capability AND to every ancestor in its delegation chain, and each ancestor's own ceiling — read from its stored record, not from the caller — must admit the increment. So an orchestrator holding 25.00 that delegates 2.00 to each of a hundred workers can still spend 25.00 in total, not 200.00. Narrowing at delegation bounds each child; this bounds the sum. An ancestor whose record is gone (Store.Purge, after expiry) no longer bounds anything — its children expired with it, since a child cannot outlive its parent. The capability itself must be on record: Bump, Charge, Reserve and Settle refuse one that is not — never recorded, or purged — with ErrNotFound, since none of its ancestors' ceilings could be read. A cost reported late is charged only while the record lasts, so keep records (PurgeRequest.ExpiredFor) as long as costs may still arrive.

##### Copies of a Biscuit

A Biscuit's holder can give a copy limits of its own (CopyCeiling), which arrive through the Subject of BumpRequest, ChargeRequest and ReserveRequest (MeterSubject.Copies). Each is counted under its capability and revocation id, apart from its siblings, and checked before the capability's ceilings; the capability's counters still take every copy's requests and spend. A charge or reservation records the copies it debited, so Refund, Settle, Release and ReleaseExpired return to them without being handed them again. A Meter that does not count copies must not be paired with a verifier that sets BiscuitConfig.MeterCopies.

A holder mints copies offline, as many as it likes, and each one metered is a counter the store keeps until the capability's usage goes. So each capability bounds the copies counted for it and for every capability delegated from it by its quota (limes.Caveats.Copies — the subject's from its token, an ancestor's from its record), as it bounds their requests and spend, and a store counts at most its own bound of copies per capability — its configuration's, or DefaultMaxCopiesPerCapability. Bump, Charge and Reserve refuse a call that would take any of these past it as ErrCopyLimitExceeded, counting nothing. A copy already counted goes on being metered, and it stays counted under the ancestors once its capability's usage is dropped (DeleteUsage, PurgeOrphans), as its requests and spend do; dropping an ancestor's own usage restarts its count with its other counters. A store keeps that count on each capability's counters rather than walking its subtree, so admitting a copy costs the length of the chain, not the size of the tree.

All methods are concurrency-safe. A rejected call mutates nothing, so a retry after rejection is safe. Each method first refuses a request whose Validate does, before it reads anything: a store that calls Validate enforces a rule added to it without a change of its own.

A store over a database holds at most one connection per call: the reads of the lineage, the ceilings and the ledger, the writes, and onCharged all run on the one transaction the call opens. A call that takes a second connection while it holds its transaction deadlocks once as many calls run as the pool has connections — each holds one and waits for another — which a large pool under a light load never shows. Run metertest against a pool of one or two connections to catch it.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.MeterReader"></a>

### meter.MeterReader

```go
type MeterReader interface {
	// GetCharge returns one charge of the ledger, by the ChargeID its
	// receipt carried — the id Refund takes. ErrChargeNotFound when there
	// is none.
	GetCharge(ctx context.Context, chargeID uuid.UUID) (ChargeRecord, error)

	// ChargeByRef returns the charge a capability took under an external
	// reference (ChargeRequest.ExternalRef), so a reporter can reconcile
	// its own records with the ledger. ErrChargeNotFound when there is none.
	// It refuses what ChargeByRefRequest.Validate refuses, an empty
	// reference among them: no charge is taken under no name.
	ChargeByRef(ctx context.Context, req ChargeByRefRequest) (ChargeRecord, error)

	// GetReservation returns a reservation still holding budget — open,
	// or expired and not yet released, since until ReleaseExpired runs it
	// still counts (ExpiresAt tells which). ErrReservationNotFound once it
	// is settled or released.
	GetReservation(ctx context.Context, reservationID uuid.UUID) (Reservation, error)

	// ListReservations returns, a page at a time, every reservation
	// GetReservation would return that was made against the capability
	// itself — not its delegated children — soonest to expire first, and
	// holds expiring at the same instant in ascending ID, compared bytewise.
	// It refuses what ListReservationsRequest.Validate refuses.
	ListReservations(ctx context.Context, req ListReservationsRequest) (limes.Page[Reservation], error)

	// GetUsage returns the current snapshot. Returns ErrUsageNotFound when no
	// row exists for the capability — typically means it's never been
	// used (no requests, no charges). For a capability with delegated
	// children the counters include the children's usage.
	GetUsage(ctx context.Context, capID uuid.UUID) (Usage, error)
}
```

MeterReader reads back what the Meter recorded: charges, reservations and counters. A reporter or an admin view depends on it alone.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.OverrunPolicyUnspecified"></a><a id="meter.OverrunPolicyReject"></a><a id="meter.OverrunPolicyRecord"></a>

#### meter.OverrunPolicyUnspecified, meter.OverrunPolicyReject, meter.OverrunPolicyRecord

```go
const (
	// OverrunPolicyUnspecified takes the default, OverrunPolicyReject: a
	// caller that says nothing never commits past a ceiling.
	OverrunPolicyUnspecified OverrunPolicy = iota
	// OverrunPolicyReject refuses the charge with the ceiling's sentinel and
	// changes nothing. Use it for a cost not yet incurred: the refusal is
	// what stops it.
	OverrunPolicyReject
	// OverrunPolicyRecord commits the charge past the ceiling and reports it in
	// ChargeReceipt.Overrun. Use it for a cost already incurred — reported
	// after the fact, out of the request path — where refusing would only
	// leave the ledger short of what was spent. The crossed ceiling then
	// refuses every later charge and reservation under OverrunPolicyReject.
	OverrunPolicyRecord
)
```

```go
type ReleaseMatchingRequest struct {

	// them in every tenant instead. Exactly one of the two is required.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// AllTenants releases the holds in every tenant, by ClientID, Session
	// and SubjectIssuer alone, as limes.RevokeMatchingRequest.AllTenants
	// revokes. It names no
	// tenant, so a call after a revocation across tenants needs no list of
	// the tenants it wrote in: one whose release failed is retried as it
	// was, though the revocation, repeated, revokes nothing.
	AllTenants bool
	// Subject, OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session, SubjectIssuer and RunID
	// select as on limes.RevokeMatchingRequest; at least one of them or
	// CapabilityID is required.
	Subject, OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session, SubjectIssuer string
	RunID                                                 uuid.UUID
	// CapabilityID selects one capability by its id, as after
	// limes.Revoker.Revoke of that one: its holds and those of the
	// capabilities delegated from it. It names one tenant's.
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	// Limit bounds the holds one call releases. Zero:
	// DefaultHousekeepingLimit; negative is refused.
	Limit int
}
```

ReleaseMatchingRequest names the holds ReleaseMatching releases: those of the revoked capabilities of one tenant, or of every tenant, that match each selector set, by the rules limes.RevokeMatchingRequest selects by, or that CapabilityID names, and of every capability delegated from one (docs/adr/0015-release-matching-holds.md).

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.RequestCounter"></a>

### meter.RequestCounter

```go
type RequestCounter interface {
	// Bump increments the request counter of the capability and of
	// each ancestor, and returns the capability's new count. When any
	// ceiling in the chain would be crossed it returns
	// ErrRequestLimitExceeded and nothing is mutated. Under a lease that
	// keeps moving while the call locks it, a store may refuse it as
	// limes.ErrConflict, mutating nothing, for the caller to send again
	// (Leaser).
	Bump(ctx context.Context, req BumpRequest) (BumpReceipt, error)
}
```

RequestCounter enforces the request ceilings (Caveats.Requests) alone, as Meter describes them: on the capability, on each ancestor still on record and on each Biscuit copy. Code that spends nothing through limes depends on it alone, and metertest.RunCounter checks a store against it.

It does not enforce Caveats.Budget. A capability whose cost is spent outside limes, beside a store held only as a RequestCounter, has no budget limes checks; meter its spend with a BudgetMeter.

### meter.Reservation

```go
type Reservation struct {
	ID           uuid.UUID
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	TenantID     uuid.UUID
	// Amount is held in UnitCode.
	Amount   limes.Nanos
	UnitCode string
	// Op and Actor are what Settle will stamp on the charge.
	Op    limes.Op
	Actor string
	// Copies are the Biscuit copies the hold is also on, innermost first,
	// with the budget each is held against.
	Copies    []HeldCopy
	ExpiresAt time.Time
	// Replayed reports that Reserve found the hold already on record under
	// its ReservationID, so the call moved nothing. Only Reserve sets it;
	// GetReservation and ListReservations never do.

}
```

Reservation is a committed hold, as Reserve made it and as GetReservation and ListReservations read it back.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.ReserveRequest"></a>

### meter.ReserveRequest

```go
type ReserveRequest struct {
	// Subject is the capability the hold counts against
	// (VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject). The reservation keeps the
	// presented copy's limits, and Settle checks and charges them.
	Subject limes.MeterSubject
	// Amount to hold, in the subject's unit. Within 0..MaxNanos
	// (Nanos.Validate).
	Amount limes.Nanos
	// TTL is how long the hold lasts if never settled or released, at most
	// until its capability expires (Meter.Reserve). 0 =
	// DefaultReservationTTL; negative is ErrInvalidRequest.
	TTL time.Duration
	// Op and Actor are carried onto the charge Settle records.
	Op    limes.Op
	Actor string
	// ReservationID is the id the hold is made under, which makes Reserve
	// idempotent on it (Meter.Reserve): the caller's own, so a Reserve sent
	// again after its answer was lost (ErrOutcomeUnknown) finds the hold
	// the first one made. The zero id: the store picks one, and every call
	// holds anew.
	ReservationID uuid.UUID
}
```

ReserveRequest is the input to Meter.Reserve.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.SetTenantBudgetRequest"></a>

### meter.SetTenantBudgetRequest

```go
type SetTenantBudgetRequest struct {
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Ceiling is the tenant's new ceiling, in the unit it names: the zero
	// value freezes the tenant's spend, in whatever unit it counts, and
	// BudgetCeiling{Unlimited: true, UnitCode: u} lifts it.
	Ceiling limes.BudgetCeiling
	// PeriodEnd pins a closing time for the accounting window; zero leaves
	// it open-ended (typical for "just set the cap, I'll roll later").
	PeriodEnd time.Time
	// ResetSpend=true zeroes the spend and rolls PeriodStart to
	// now. false leaves the counter alone — the cap changes mid-
	// window.
	ResetSpend bool
	// ExpectedVersion is the optimistic-concurrency guard, checked
	// atomically with the write. 0 asserts no ceiling has been set yet (the
	// budget is missing, or holds only counted spend) and is itself a
	// conflict if one has, so two operators editing one ceiling cannot
	// overwrite each other unseen.
	ExpectedVersion int64
}
```

SetTenantBudgetRequest is the input for UsageStore.SetTenantBudget.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>

A store calls it before reading the tenant's row, so a malformed request is refused as one, never as a version conflict.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.StoreEvents"></a>

### meter.StoreEvents

```go
type StoreEvents struct {
	// OnTenantWait is called each time a metered call has locked the row
	// of its tenant's aggregate, or written the tenant's stripe where the
	// store counts a tenant with no ceiling in stripes, however short the
	// wait: a histogram needs the fast samples too.
	OnTenantWait func(context.Context, TenantWaitEvent)
}
```

StoreEvents are the callbacks a usage store makes as it works, for metrics beside its log (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md, Decision 6). Each is optional: a nil one drops its events without a word. A store that has nothing to report for one never calls it.

They run synchronously, on the caller's goroutine, while the call runs, mostly inside its open transaction with its locks held: a callback must not block, and must not panic — the store does not recover one. Fields may be added to the struct and to its events.

<a id="meter.TenantBudget"></a>

### meter.TenantBudget

```go
type TenantBudget struct {
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Ceiling bounds the tenant's spend in the current period, in the unit
	// the tenant counts in: Ceiling.UnitCode, which the first charge or
	// hold records when no ceiling named it. A tenant whose ceiling was
	// never set counts Unlimited.
	Ceiling     limes.BudgetCeiling
	SpentAmount limes.Nanos
	// ReservedAmount is held by the tenant's open reservations.
	ReservedAmount limes.Nanos
	PeriodStart    time.Time
	// PeriodEnd is when the accounting window closes; zero for an
	// open-ended one.
	PeriodEnd time.Time
	// UpdatedAt is when the store last wrote the aggregate, by its clock.
	UpdatedAt time.Time
	// ResourceVersion is the OCC token a caller passes back as
	// SetTenantBudgetRequest.ExpectedVersion. Zero means no ceiling has
	// ever been set — the row, if there is one, holds only what Charge and
	// Reserve counted.
	ResourceVersion int64
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

TenantBudget is the snapshot view of the tenant aggregate cap. Amounts are Nanos, exact; a store keeps them exactly too (an integer or decimal column), so that sums do not drift.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantBudget.Utilization"></a>

#### meter.TenantBudget.Utilization

```go
func (b TenantBudget) Utilization() (pct float64, limited bool)
```

Utilization is how much of the ceiling is spent, in percent, clamped to 0..100: a tenant past its ceiling, or with a ceiling of 0, is at 100. limited is false for an unlimited tenant, which has no utilization to report; pct is then 0.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantBudgetBusyError"></a>

### meter.TenantBudgetBusyError

```go
type TenantBudgetBusyError struct {
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Waited is how long the store waited before it gave up.
	Waited time.Duration
	// Holders is how many transactions held the tenant's calls in flight
	// when it gave up.
	Holders int
	// Oldest is the longest running of the holders the store's database
	// role may inspect; nil when it may inspect none. PostgreSQL shows a
	// session of another role only to one granted pg_read_all_stats, so a
	// holder of another service's role is counted in Holders and seen no
	// further.
	Oldest *TenantBudgetHolder
}
```

TenantBudgetBusyError is ErrTenantBudgetBusy with what the store saw of the calls it waited for, so a caller can tell a tenant's ordinary load, which a retry outlasts, from a call held open, which no retry outlasts until it ends. errors.Is matches ErrTenantBudgetBusy, and limes answers it by that code.

<a id="meter.TenantBudgetLister"></a>

### meter.TenantBudgetLister

```go
type TenantBudgetLister interface {
	// ListTenantBudgets returns one page (TenantBudgets.ListTenantBudgets).
	ListTenantBudgets(ctx context.Context, req ListTenantBudgetsRequest) (limes.Page[TenantBudget], error)
}
```

TenantBudgetLister lists tenant budgets a page at a time. Every TenantBudgets is one.

<sub>[meter/pages.go](../../meter/pages.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantBudgets"></a>

### meter.TenantBudgets

```go
type TenantBudgets interface {
	// GetTenantBudget returns the tenant-aggregate snapshot. Returns
	// ErrTenantBudgetNotFound when no row exists (tenant has no cap
	// configured AND has never been charged).
	//
	// The aggregate counts from the tenant's first charge or reservation,
	// whether or not a ceiling has been set: Charge and Reserve create the
	// row, with no ceiling and ResourceVersion 0, when it is missing. A
	// ceiling set afterwards is measured against that spend and those holds.
	GetTenantBudget(ctx context.Context, tenantID uuid.UUID) (TenantBudget, error)

	// SetTenantBudget upserts the tenant cap. ResetSpend=true rolls
	// the accounting period and zeroes the spend — operators call
	// this on each billing close. ResetSpend=false adjusts the cap
	// mid-cycle without affecting accumulated spend. It refuses what
	// SetTenantBudgetRequest.Validate refuses — a ceiling outside
	// 0..MaxNanos is ErrInvalidAmount — and changes nothing. A ceiling in a
	// unit other than the row's returns ErrUnitCodeMismatch while anything
	// is held in the old unit, or spent in it and not reset. A reset settles
	// the tenant's leases first; a store that cannot keep new ones out
	// meanwhile may refuse it as limes.ErrConflict, changing nothing, and
	// the caller tries again.
	SetTenantBudget(ctx context.Context, req SetTenantBudgetRequest) (TenantBudget, error)

	// ListTenantBudgets returns tenant budget rows; a consumer joins its
	// own tenant data to them by TenantID. Filter picks the rows:
	//   - TenantBudgetFilterUnspecified, TenantBudgetFilterAll: every one.
	//   - TenantBudgetFilterAtOrPast: rows with a ceiling — a bound or 0 — where
	//     spent * BasisPointsPerWhole >= max * ThresholdBasisPoints, in
	//     integers; a ceiling of 0 is
	//     spent through at any threshold. At a threshold of 0, every row
	//     with a ceiling.
	//   - TenantBudgetFilterUnlimited: rows whose ceiling is Unlimited.
	// Limit is the page size, as PageLimit reads it.
	// It refuses what ListTenantBudgetsRequest.Validate refuses, and a store
	// that scopes tenants refuses with ErrScopeMismatch a call whose scope
	// admits fewer than every tenant, as CountRecords does: under it the
	// page would read as every tenant's while it showed fewer.
	//
	// Rows come most at risk first. Ceilings of 0, which allow nothing,
	// lead; bounded ceilings follow by spent / max descending, compared
	// exactly as fractions — unclamped, so of two tenants past their
	// ceilings the further one leads; unlimited ceilings, with no utilization, trail. Within each,
	// ties go by tenant id. A page ends with a cursor that fetches
	// the next one, empty on the last page. Spend moves between pages, so
	// a tenant may show on two of them, or on none; a cursor is a place in
	// the order, not a snapshot.
	ListTenantBudgets(ctx context.Context, req ListTenantBudgetsRequest) (limes.Page[TenantBudget], error)
}
```

TenantBudgets administers the tenant-aggregate ceilings Charge enforces.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantReservationLister"></a>

### meter.TenantReservationLister

```go
type TenantReservationLister interface {
	// ListTenantReservations returns, a page at a time, every reservation
	// of req.TenantID's capabilities that GetReservation would return —
	// open, or expired and not yet released — soonest to expire first, and
	// holds expiring at the same instant in ascending ID, compared
	// bytewise: ListReservations' order. Their amounts sum to the tenant's
	// ReservedAmount at one instant; each page is read on its own, so a
	// walk of many is no snapshot. It refuses what
	// ListTenantReservationsRequest.Validate refuses, and a call scoped to
	// another tenant as limes.ErrScopeMismatch.
	ListTenantReservations(ctx context.Context, req ListTenantReservationsRequest) (limes.Page[Reservation], error)
}
```

TenantReservationLister lists the holds that count against a tenant's budget, for an operator who sees TenantBudget.ReservedAmount and asks which holds make it up. It is separate from MeterReader so that a usage store of the consumer's own implements nothing more; memstore's and pgstore's do, and metertest checks it when the store under test is one.

<sub>[meter/tenant_reservations.go](../../meter/tenant_reservations.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantUsageEraser"></a>

### meter.TenantUsageEraser

```go
type TenantUsageEraser interface {
	// EraseTenantUsage removes every counter, hold and charge of the
	// tenant's capabilities and its Biscuit copies, and the tenant's
	// aggregate: the charges ledger is the tenant's billing history, and
	// it does not come back. It changes no other tenant's rows.
	//
	// It also marks the tenant erased, so that a call made after it — a
	// request verified before the erase, a late cost — counts nothing of
	// the tenant again: Bump, Charge, Reserve and SetTenantBudget for it
	// return ErrTenantErased, and so does the limes.Store's Insert. PurgeOrphans forgets the mark once none of the
	// tenant's records is left, and with it any call that could be metered.
	//
	// It returns what it removed (EraseTenantUsageResult).
	EraseTenantUsage(ctx context.Context, req EraseTenantUsageRequest) (EraseTenantUsageResult, error)
}
```

TenantUsageEraser is a UsageStore that erases one tenant's usage, for a consumer removing the tenant. It is optional; metertest checks a UsageStore that implements it.

<sub>[meter/erase.go](../../meter/erase.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.TenantWaitEvent"></a>

### meter.TenantWaitEvent

```go
type TenantWaitEvent struct {
	// TenantID is the tenant whose aggregate the call locked.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Operation is the store call that locked it.
	Operation StoreOperation
	// Wait is how long locking the row took, or writing the stripe, by the
	// database's clock: the wait for that row alone, not for the tenant's
	// advisory lock nor for the counters of the call's chain. Never
	// negative.
	Wait time.Duration
}
```

TenantWaitEvent is one wait of a metered call for its tenant's aggregate.

<sub>[meter/events.go](../../meter/events.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.Usage"></a>

### meter.Usage

```go
type Usage struct {
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	RequestCount int64
	SpentAmount  limes.Nanos
	// ReservedAmount is held by open reservations (its subtree's, for a
	// capability with delegated children).
	ReservedAmount limes.Nanos
	// ReservedRequests is held by open leases (Leaser): the requests a
	// lease of the capability's, or of one below it, holds and has not yet
	// made, or not yet settled. A Bump not under a lease counts them
	// against the ceiling as made.
	ReservedRequests int64
	// UnitCode is the unit the counters count in: the subject's, recorded
	// by the first Bump, Charge or Reserve of a subject that names one, so
	// a capability that has only been bumped reads its unit too. Empty
	// while none has.
	UnitCode string
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Usage is the snapshot view of a capability's runtime counters.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.UsageHousekeeping"></a>

### meter.UsageHousekeeping

```go
type UsageHousekeeping interface {
	// DeleteUsage drops the capability's row and the counters of its Biscuit
	// copies. Called when the capability is reaped: on a capability still on
	// record it restarts the capability's own counters, and its ceilings with
	// them, from zero — PurgeOrphans drops only the rows of records gone. It releases the
	// capability's open reservations first,
	// returning their holds to its ancestors and its tenant: nothing could
	// settle or release them afterwards. A capability with no row is no
	// error: there is nothing to drop. It settles the leases of the
	// capability and of those below it first; a store that cannot keep new
	// ones out meanwhile may refuse it as limes.ErrConflict, dropping
	// nothing, and the caller tries again. It refuses what
	// DeleteUsageRequest.Validate refuses.
	DeleteUsage(ctx context.Context, req DeleteUsageRequest) error

	// PurgeOrphans deletes the usage rows of capabilities no longer on
	// record (Store.Purge), with their copies' counters, releasing their
	// reservations as DeleteUsage does, at
	// most req.Limit of them (HousekeepingLimit); the caller loops while a
	// batch comes back full. It refuses what PurgeOrphansRequest.Validate
	// refuses.
	PurgeOrphans(ctx context.Context, req PurgeOrphansRequest) (PurgeOrphansResult, error)

	// ReleaseExpired releases the reservations past their expiry, at most
	// req.Limit of them (HousekeepingLimit), refusing what
	// ReleaseExpiredRequest.Validate refuses; a hold expires with its capability at the latest
	// (Meter.Reserve). A revoked capability's hold is not released early: it
	// can still be settled, as a cost already incurred belongs in the ledger
	// (StoredMeterSubject). Run on a timer: until it runs, an expired hold
	// keeps counting against the ceilings, which errs towards refusing
	// spend, never towards allowing too much.
	ReleaseExpired(ctx context.Context, req ReleaseExpiredRequest) (ReleaseExpiredResult, error)
}
```

UsageHousekeeping reclaims usage rows of capabilities that are gone.

<sub>[meter/usage.go](../../meter/usage.go)</sub>
<a id="meter.UsageStore"></a>

### meter.UsageStore

```go
type UsageStore interface {
	Meter
	MeterReader
	TenantBudgets
	UsageHousekeeping
}
```

UsageStore is everything a consumer implements for runtime accounting. It is the union of narrower contracts so that code which only meters (an interceptor, a handler) can depend on Meter alone — on RequestCounter when it counts requests and spends nothing — a reporter on MeterReader, and code which only administers tenant ceilings on TenantBudgets.

##### A call whose answer is lost

A store over a database can lose the answer to a call after the call's commit has left: the connection drops, or the context ends, before the database replies. Such a call returns an error matching ErrOutcomeUnknown, beside its cause: it may have committed or not, and the store cannot tell. Only a call keyed to its cost is safe to send again — Charge with an ExternalRef, Reserve with a ReservationID, Refund with a RefundID, and Settle, keyed to its reservation: a repeat of one that committed replays it and moves nothing, and a repeat of one that did not commits it now. An unkeyed call sent again may count twice; one not sent again may never count. A store that commits in memory never returns it.

##### Growth from 1.0

UsageStore's method set, and that of each interface it is made of, is frozen at 1.0: a method added to an interface breaks every store written against it. A capability added later arrives as an interface of its own, optional, which a caller discovers by a type assertion on the store, as Leaser, CopyUsageReader and TenantUsageEraser are.
